title: Calibration decisions after lunch
status: National housing geography adopted for documents; other target definitions and weights remain open
summary: Keep the 2007 stationary reference and most of the existing target construction. The completed review does not justify rebuilding the July strategy. The main first-birth housing comparison does need a common measurement rule before it can support an adopted calibration.

Decisions on fertility, wealth and housing levels can be made now. The first-birth diagnostic is a separate calculation from saved policies and must not hold up those decisions. Confidence flags below assess measurement comparability, not how well a selected model fits.

The present reference combines 2004/2006 CPS fertility stocks, 2003-2006 natality timing, 2003/2005 PSID wealth and national 2005/2006 ACS housing. These are nearby-year measurements used for a stationary 2007 economy, not one identical population observed in 2007.

decisions.recommendation: The author has selected the current 2007 reference with national US housing targets. The four national housing values replace the prior 42-metro document values for the next comparison.
decisions.evidence: The verified national values are mean rooms 5.607885960068579, ownership 0.6762604168538028, family rooms 0.38509964969278165 and recent-parent ownership gap 0.12760836356692162.
decisions.alternative: The former 42-metro document values remain historical comparison values; they are not the current selected housing population.
decisions.consequence: The selected national ownership target is higher than the former 42-metro target. This decision does not by itself explain model fit.
decisions.next_operation: Defer loss calculation and rescoring until the next run. Record the complete national target/weight contract before that comparison.

decisions.recommendation: Keep both CPS shares, both grouped NCHS timing targets and the separately imposed 2.1 normalization. Use one stated within-cell timing convention; retain the implemented uniform-time approximation for now.
decisions.evidence: The empirical scalars and implemented age mapping reproduce. Mean first-birth age 25.9763 is the data mapped to model age cells, not an arithmetic error. Raw recorded-age mean 25.1608 is a different object. The 2.1 anchor concerns age-46+ mean children ever born and is not a measured period TFR.
decisions.alternative: Adopt a different birth-time or maternal-age-support convention jointly for data and model. Do not replace the grouped mean with the raw mean while leaving its model observer unchanged.
decisions.consequence: The model approximates one reproductive household member and within-cell age exposure. Accepting that approximation permits decisions now; it does not certify exact female survey exposure.
decisions.next_operation: Write the accepted population, age and timing conventions into the contract. Recompute only if a different convention is chosen.

decisions.recommendation: Retain the three signed-off economic objects: aggregate wealth/gross earnings, annual bequests/wealth and living-old wealth-to-income dispersion. Keep the existing scalar values for this comparison.
decisions.evidence: The July review explicitly selected these objects. Current arithmetic reproduces. The bequest weight is a chosen 5% tolerance, not a sampling standard error. Constant modeled pension income makes the model's old-age wealth and wealth/income percentile ratios coincide.
decisions.alternative: If the intended third object is pure wealth dispersion, choose the already measured same-sample levels ratio 4.919429 (SE 0.579804), replacing the current wealth/income ratio 3.515935 (SE 0.306911). This is a conceptual choice, not a mandatory code correction.
decisions.consequence: Retaining the current dispersion accepts omitted retirement-income heterogeneity as a measurement approximation. Neither option fixes or validates the entrant-wealth mapping.
decisions.next_operation: No new data audit is needed to retain these rows. A chosen levels-dispersion alternative can be rescored on saved model values under a separately named contract.

decisions.decision: Children in the family-room and recent-parent rows
decisions.recommendation: Retain the current selected national resident-own-child family-room row and the national recent-parent ownership row, with the existing stock-versus-flow qualification for recent parents. The minor-child definition remains a proposed choice pending discussion.
decisions.evidence: The national family-room target is 0.38509964969278165 and the national recent-parent ownership gap is 0.12760836356692162. The linked-minor 0.336220 candidate was measured for 42 metros, not nationally.
decisions.alternative: A national linked-minor candidate has not yet been measured. The existing 42-metro minor-child candidate is not a national alternative.
decisions.consequence: The population choice does not silently alter the child grouping. Minor age and stochastic model dependence are still not exactly the same object.
decisions.next_operation: Defer loss calculation and rescoring until the next run. An exact recent-child-age comparison remains separate saved-policy measurement work.

decisions.recommendation: Keep the original PSID regression as empirical evidence; require an explicitly matched auxiliary statistic on data and simulated model histories before adopting this row as evidence for one utility specification.
decisions.evidence: The 0.720246 target and clustered SE 0.085260 reproduce exactly. The current scored model contrast instead compares two branches from the same pre-birth households at the next model date, permitting another birth only in the treated branch. These are different estimators.
decisions.alternative: Explicitly accept the current forced-branch comparison as a provisional approximation. It must not be described as the identical PSID regression or used to claim that a housing mechanism is rejected by the data.
decisions.consequence: A longer empirical window, division by two, or a favorable timing projection is not an automatic correction. Preserve this identifying information for the housing-preference block; do not drop the row simply because it is difficult to fit.
decisions.next_operation: Declare birth/interview timing, sample, joint observation histories, controls and weights on both sides before calculating the candidate fit. If education is absent from the model, any reduced empirical regression must drop it on the data side too and be labeled a new candidate. The lunch calculation only exposes origin and destination branch responses.

decisions.recommendation: Treat weighting and uncertainty as open decisions for the national population. The frozen weights remain historical comparison weights and are not adopted for the new population.
decisions.evidence: Scales mix empirical sampling uncertainty, annual temporal variation and an external bequest tolerance; cross-moment covariance is not used. The floor estimates nine structural coordinates, the shares alternative ten, with fertility utility normalized separately.
decisions.alternative: Choose a weighting rule on substantive grounds, name the full replacement contract and preserve all affected identifying information. A new rule is not a revision of old scores.
decisions.consequence: A lower loss is useful search evidence but not an efficient-SMM test, identification proof or numerical-convergence certificate.
decisions.next_operation: Defer loss calculation and rescoring until the next run. Revisit utility only after that comparison; new behavioral solutions are needed for a refit, not for a purely scalar target rescore.

other_decisions: Entry wealth: retain heterogeneity and the reviewed 18-24 childless-renter proxy. The running inherited law and the new common-income-scale candidate are different laws. The candidate has positive current renter slack, but no full continuation/equilibrium validation or adoption. Choose units explicitly before a new refit; zero entry is not the baseline recommendation.

External housing depreciation: the inspected serialized input uses 1.1% annually; the slides say 2%. Existing comparisons use 1.1%. Reconcile this restriction before a new refit; a change would require new solutions, not target rescoring. No silent model change is made here.
Parameter connections in the table describe informative economic margins, not one-to-one identification. Fixed borrowing, earnings and housing restrictions affect many of these moments.

first_birth_diagnostic.status: Two complete fixed-policy measurements; original scored D1 reproduced exactly in both
first_birth_diagnostic.estimator: Same-origin successful-first-birth households, cloned into a birth branch and a childless control; stationary saved policy at origin and four years later. No empirical regression is simulated.
paragraphs: The immediate response is already 0.903 rooms under the selected floor and 0.997 under selected child-dependent shares. Four years later the corresponding responses are 0.987 and 1.044. Moving the native reading from the destination date to the origin reduces the response by only 0.085 and 0.046 rooms, respectively.

These calculations establish that most of this model branch response occurs at the birth decision. They do not establish that the empirical miss survives a common estimator: the PSID coefficient contrast uses different comparison households, timing, controls and weights. Neither native date is automatically the empirical -1/+3 contrast.

Both cases use persistent earnings with 15 income states and inherited heterogeneous entry wealth, but are separately recalibrated selected points. Their difference cannot be attributed to utility alone. Each destination response reproduces its original scored value exactly; the full contracts and checkpoint identities were checked. No new household or equilibrium was solved.

The returned mass checks pass unchanged. The floor has zero destination projection mass; the shares case has tiny recorded projections around 1.55e-167, not exactly zero. This measurement replay adds no grid-convergence or continuation-value certificate.
first_birth_diagnostic.plot_caption: Supplemental diagnostic only. Dashed segments connect two model dates; no annual path or birth-date interpolation is assumed. This is not an overlay of the PSID event-study coefficients. The standard 17 plots per selected case remain unchanged.
